analysis.title: Energy, Utilities & Mining Pulse: Investors Asking: What Has Been the Strongest & Weakest Mid/Large Cap Performer Over the Past Month?
key_insights: GS names a strongest and weakest mid/large cap performer over the past month in seven sub-sectors: MPC/CVE (integrated oils and refining), HAL/MTZ (energy services), KMI/HESM (midstream), OVV/DVN (E&P), TLN/NRG (utilities), VLTO/OKLO (clean tech), CLF/FCX (metals and mining).

MPC was the strongest refiner on elevated margins. September blended crack was $53.81/bbl vs $33.54/bbl in 2Q26, wider light-heavy differentials from surging dirty freight rates, and 2027 FactSet consensus EPS up ~26% in a month. MPC says each $1/bbl of wider sour differentials adds about $520 mn annual EBITDA in R&M. GS PT $519, ~14% total return.

CVE lagged on wider WTI-WCS differentials and profit-taking after a strong year. GS still sees the highest total return potential in Canadian oil coverage, with first oil at West White Rose expected imminently and a fifth OTSG start-up at Christina Lake. The planned Athabasca Oil acquisition around year-end could temporarily pressure the balance sheet. Management targets C$4 bn long-term net debt, after which returns step up to 100% of excess free funds flow.

HAL recovered after a softer 2Q outlook. In-line 3Q26 results and 2027 commentary show earnings can grow in flat North America activity. GS sees mid-single-digit 2027 revenue growth in a base case and HAL at a ~2x discount to SLB on 2028 estimates.

MTZ lagged on the sell-off in AI and power-related equities and project push-outs in Communications and Pipelines. Management guided lower Communications earnings for 2H26. GS calls the sell-off overdone and stays constructive on grid, power generation and data center work.

KMI led midstream after a larger-than-expected backlog increase at 3Q earnings, including the Southeast Connector (+2.6 bcf/d, $3.1b net capex) and Permian Link (+2.8 bcf/d, $1.6b net capex). Both could be upsized. GS is below consensus EBITDA and watches 2027 guidance in December.

HESM was the weakest midstream name after restructuring its contracts with sponsor Chevron, a planned separation from CVX, and another 2026 guidance cut. CVX gets a ~50% cut in Bakken G&P fees per unit and $200m cash. HESM gets CVX's Rockies midstream assets and CVX's ~40% equity stake. The stock fell ~15% on the news and another 7-8% afterward. Investors flag FCF/share dilution, lower growth and higher leverage.

OVV (+19%) was the strongest large cap E&P on Permian execution (surfactant program), outperformance versus a re-rating forward WTI curve (+12%/+8% for 2027/2028), and eligibility for TSX Composite inclusion after S&P's September 11 criteria change.

DVN (+6%) was the weakest large cap E&P ahead of 3Q26 as investors wait on the portfolio review after the $4.2 bn Eagle Ford sale to Crescent Energy. GS sees a 14% FCF yield on average 2027/2028 estimates vs 10% for large cap peers (FANG, EOG, OXY, COP).

TLN (+16%) led utilities and IPPs on a buyback increase to $3bn including a $1.5bn accelerated share repurchase, higher PJM power prices, and CEG's two PPAs covering ~19% of its nuclear fleet. NRG (-5%) lagged on PJM strength versus weaker Texas pricing, slower data center contracting confidence and 2027 earnings visibility. NRG trades at ~15.3% FCF yield vs 11.4% for coverage ex-CEG.

VLTO (+7%) led clean tech on consistent execution and Water Quality strength. OKLO (-27%) lagged on higher rates, capital intensity of its build-own-operate model, a general nuclear pullback, and PJM's rejection of its interconnection request. GS stays cautious on OKLO.

CLF (+15%) led metals on a better 2027 outlook from higher US and Canadian steel pricing, contract renegotiations effective 1Q27, and a blast furnace reline pushed to 2028 (about 500kt extra 2027 output per GS). GS stays cautious because the outlook needs sustained higher prices, costs are rising and USW negotiations could add costs.

FCX (-5%) lagged on macro concerns, copper pulling back from highs amid inflation and rate worries, higher diesel costs, and Indonesia El Nino water-scarcity questions for mills. GS remains constructive on structural copper demand and the Grasberg ramp.

Midstream and power: VG's data center power expansion draws mixed investor feedback. Bulls like the BKR/GEV equipment agreement as a low-cost call option. Bears cite weak power contracting, competition, and a possible slip of the cash flow inflection from late this decade to early next. DTM investors recalibrate growth around a phased MIST expansion.

Utilities: nuclear questions rose after AEP's JDA with X-Energy in Indiana (~960 MW feasibility). Investors favor large AP1000 reactors over SMRs. November elections put GA, OH, PA and TX in focus, with Ohio too close to call, creating caution on AEP and FE. Investors expect state data center incentives to be reduced or eliminated.

Energy services and gas: LBRT signed a 1.2 GW integrated power agreement with a frontier AI lab, with the first ESA (~500 MW) targeted for December 2026. AESI secured bridge financing for two data center power projects with first power in late 2027. Gas E&Ps face 3Q26 sales revisions on weak Appalachian in-basin pricing. EXE is down ~16% YTD and is hedged 66%/46% for 2026/2027.

Majors and refiners: XOM's 8-K implies EPS around $4.10 excluding timing effects and identified items, with better Downstream. Investors are defensive ahead of majors' 3Q26 results next week. VLO reported better-than-expected EPS on refining. Bulls see stronger Q4 revisions and bears cite YTD outperformance and valuation.

Sector context: the 10-year yield at 4.9% is a headwind for utilities (XLU has underperformed SPY this year). E&Ps imply a cost of capital above 11%. Global average crude freight rates surged above $20/bbl last week from $3/bbl a year ago, with Middle East routes above $35/bbl.

sector_views.rationale: Elevated cracks, wider light-heavy differentials and upward 2027 revisions support refiners. Buy CVX and COP into 3Q26 results per GS preview.
Improving North America pricing, international activity gains and behind-the-meter power contracts.
Gas pipeline backlogs are growing and the gas/power macro outlook is described as constructive, with HESM a Sell exception.
E&Ps imply a cost of capital above 11% and WTI slightly below the five-year strip. Sentiment on US natural gas into winter remains soft.
A 4.9% 10-year yield weighs on utility multiples. PJM power prices and data center contracting support IPPs, with election policy risk in GA, OH, PA and TX.
Nuclear stocks weak despite positive demand announcements. Higher rates hurt capital-intensive models.

earnings_insights: KMI 3Q26 (reported this week) was a beat and raise per GS First Take, with a backlog addition above $5b ahead of expectations. GS EBITDA is below consensus for 2027 and 2027 guidance comes in December.
HAL 3Q26 (reported this week) was in line with GS. The 2027 operating margin guide was slightly above consensus.
VLO 3Q26 (reported 10/22) EPS was better than expected on refining. The report cites reported EPS of $23.90 and GS First Take calls it a strong beat.
XOM 3Q26 EPS is not yet reported. The 8-K trading update implies EPS around $4.10 excluding timing effects and identified items, above consensus per GS. Full results come next week.
CLF 3Q26 earnings (reported this week) were a beat per GS First Take. The results pointed to a better-than-anticipated 2027 outlook, but GS stays Neutral.
STLD 3Q26 (reported this week) showed a temporary aluminum shipment miss against strong steel pricing. GS reiterates Buy.
LBRT 3Q26 EBITDA was in line with GS. NEE 3Q26 beat GS and consensus with 3.7 GW of backlog added at NEER. PCG 3Q26 EPS was in line with GS and Street. WFRD 3Q26 EBITDA was stronger than GS.
MPC 2027 FactSet consensus EPS estimates rose ~26% over the past month. Further positive revisions are expected.
HESM cut 2026 guidance again. Little new color is expected at 3Q26 earnings and formal 2027 guidance typically comes early next year.

Upcoming: EQT, EXE, RRC and AR report next week and US majors report 3Q26 next week. Investors watch TLN's 3Q call for possible number raises and NRG's 3Q update for Texas and data center commentary. VLTO's 3Q print is the next catalyst.
EXE is 66%/46% hedged on gas volumes for 2026/2027 as of 2Q26 results and targets ~$750 mn of incremental free cash flow over 3-5 years.

tension_points.bull_case: Better 2027 outlook from higher US and Canadian steel prices, contract renegotiations effective 1Q27, and a blast furnace reline pushed to 2028 adding about 500kt of 2027 output per GS.
tension_points.bear_case: The outlook relies on sustained higher prices through the entire year while costs are guided up and USW negotiations could produce a larger cost headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Steel prices failing to hold higher through the year or USW negotiations producing a larger-than-expected cost increase.

tension_points.bull_case: PJM strength, long-term fundamentals and a ~15.3% FCF yield vs 11.4% coverage average.
tension_points.bear_case: Weaker Texas pricing, moderating confidence in data center deal timing amid elections and Batch Zero process uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lack of greater visibility on 2027 earnings and progress on data center contracting would keep sentiment from improving.

tension_points.bull_case: Broad buy-in that VG can execute construction if contracts and funding are secured, and the BKR/GEV equipment agreement works like a call option with limited upfront capital.
tension_points.bear_case: Weak power contracting for several months, intense competition from players active more than a year longer, and the cash flow inflection could slip from late this decade to early next.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Contract announcements and funding plan details from management would resolve the debate, but management says details will not come until contracts are finalized.
